hints: Notice the repeat unit still contains a C=C double bond, so this cannot be a simple addition of two ordinary alkenes.
Split the six-carbon repeat into a two-carbon part, $\text{CH}_2\text{CHCl}$, and a four-carbon part, $\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CHCH}_2$.
Recall how a diene with two double bonds can add at its 1 and 4 positions to leave one double bond in the middle of the chain.
walkthrough:
**Recognise the polymer type**

Think addition polymerisation, not condensation. No small molecule is lost, double bonds in monomers simply open to join together.

Rule:
$$\text{C=C} \rightarrow \text{-C-C-}$$

**Find the chloro-containing monomer**

The first part of the repeat is $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHCl}-$. This is exactly what you get when chloroethene adds.

$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCl} \rightarrow \text{-CH}_2-\text{CHCl-}$$

**Find the unsaturated four-carbon part**

The second part is $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH=CH-CH}_2-$. This still has a double bond, so it must come from a molecule with two double bonds.

Buta-1,3-diene undergoes 1,4-addition:
$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH-CH=CH}_2 \rightarrow \text{-CH}_2-\text{CH=CH-CH}_2-$$

**Join the two together**

Putting the two addition fragments side by side gives the full repeat unit:
$$\text{-CH}_2-\text{CHCl-CH}_2-\text{CH=CH-CH}_2-$$
That matches the question exactly, so the copolymer is made from chloroethene and buta-1,3-diene.

options.A: CH2=CH2 would polymerise to give only $-CH2-CH2-$. That fragment is fully saturated and cannot explain the $-CH=CH-$ double bond seen in the repeat unit.
options.B: CH2=CHCl gives $-CH2-CHCl-$ by normal addition, and CH2=CH-CH=CH2 gives $-CH2-CH=CH-CH2-$ by 1,4-addition. Together they make exactly $-(CH2-CHCl-CH2-CH=CH-CH2)-$.
options.C: CH3-CH2Cl has no C=C double bond, so it cannot undergo addition polymerisation at all. Monomers for addition polymers must be unsaturated.
options.D: CH3-CH=CH-CH3 is but-2-ene with only one double bond. Its addition would give a saturated $-CH(CH3)-CH(CH3)-$ unit, not the $-CH2-CH=CH-CH2-$ unit with a central double bond.
